nodes.action: migrated the schema without a backup
the corruption spread to the backups and took days to repair
took a full snapshot before the migration
the migration could always be rolled back
set up point-in-time recovery snapshots independent of the backup
deployed without running the test suite
set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests
switched to continuous replication since snapshots went stale by deploy time

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Morning, Marcus. You got a sec? I need to talk about the customer DB migration I ran last night.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Uh oh. That tone usually means something went sideways. What happened?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: So... I migrated the schema without taking a backup first. I know, I know. I was in a hurry and thought the migration script was bulletproof.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Priya. You know the rule. No backup, no migration. Please tell me nothing broke.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: It broke. The migration corrupted a bunch of customer records — addresses and order histories got scrambled. And it gets worse.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Worse than corrupted production data? How?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: The corruption spread to our nightly backups before anyone noticed. It took the team three days to repair everything. I'm honestly still cleaning up the mess.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Three days. Okay. We need to talk about what we're going to do differently, because this can't happen again.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Agreed. I've already set up point-in-time recovery snapshots that are independent of the regular backup pipeline. So even if the backups get corrupted, we have a separate recovery path.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a start. But I want to see a full snapshot taken before any future migration, no exceptions.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Absolutely. I'll make that a hard requirement. And I'll document it so nobody else makes the same mistake I did.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, Priya. I saw you pushed a big change to the checkout service this morning. Did you run the test suite first?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Honestly? No. I deployed without running the tests. I was confident the change was small and isolated.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Priya, we literally just had the migration disaster. You can't keep skipping the basics.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I know. And I already regret it — a regression slipped into production. Some users are seeing a broken discount code field. It's live right now.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: How did that get past code review?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: It didn't get past review — it never went through review. I pushed straight to main and deployed. That's on me.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay. We're fixing this properly. I'm setting up a CI gate that blocks any merge unless the test suite passes. No exceptions, no manual override.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Good. I'll help you configure it. And I want to add a rule that untested code never reaches production — not even for a hotfix.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Deal. Let's get that gate live today, and then we'll roll back the checkout change and run the tests properly.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Marcus, I need to tell you something about the snapshot approach I've been using.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The full snapshot before migrations? I thought that was working well.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: It worked for the migration itself, but turns out that wasn't enough. I took a full snapshot before the last deploy, but by the time we actually deployed, the snapshot was already stale — new writes had come in during the deploy window.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So if something had gone wrong, you would have rolled back to a state that was missing recent customer activity?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. I was wrong about the snapshot being sufficient. It gave us a false sense of security.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So what are you doing instead?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: We replaced the full-snapshot approach with continuous replication. I set up a live replica that streams every write to a separate cluster in real time. That way, if we ever need to roll back, we can restore to any point in time — not just the moment the snapshot was taken.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a much better safety net. So the snapshot is gone entirely?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: We keep a daily snapshot for long-term archival, but for rollback purposes, continuous replication is the primary mechanism now. The snapshots went stale by deploy time, so they're no longer the thing we rely on.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. I'm glad you caught that before we had another incident. And the CI gate is holding up?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, no untested code has reached production since we set it up. That part is solid.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Then we're in a much better place than two weeks ago. Let's keep it that way.
